Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Rawaaha (RA) and Hadhrat Hassaan (RA) Weep when Allaah Revealed the Verse: "Only deviant people follow the poets"

Hadhrat Abul Hasan the freed slave of the Banu Naufal tribe reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Rawaaha (RA) and Hadhrat Hassaan bin Thaabit (RA) (both acclaimed poets) came weeping to Rasulullaah ﷺ when Allaah revealed Surah TaaSeenMeem Shu'araa. Rasulullaah ﷺ recited to them the verses:

blocks.arabic_text: وَالشُّعَرَآءُ يَتَّبِعُهُمُ الْغَاوٗنَ ۝ أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّهُمْ فِيْ كُلِّ وَادٍ يَّهِيْمُوْنَ ۝ وَأَنَّهُمْ يَقُوْلُوْنَ مَا لَا يَفْعَلُوْنَ ۝ إِلَّا الَّذِيْنَ اٰمَنُوْا وَعَمِلُوا الصّٰلِحٰتِ وَذَكَرُوا اللّٰهَ كَثِيْرًا وَّانْتَصَرُوْا مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا ظُلِمُوْا
blocks.text: Only deviant people follow the poets (by repeating those poems of theirs that contain rambling speech and useless talk). Do you not see that they (poets) wander lost (distracted) in every valley (have no direction and tend to sway to the extremes)? And (do you not see) that they say things which they never do? (Such is the condition of all poets) Except those who have Imaan, who do good acts, who remember Allaah abundantly and who avenge themselves after being oppressed (by counteracting the satirical poetry that the Kuffaar direct at Islaam and at Rasulullaah ﷺ with poetry of their own).

When Rasulullaah ﷺ recited the verse "Except those who have Imaan, who do good acts ", he said, "That refers to you." Thereafter, when he recited "who remember Allaah abundantly", he again said, "That refers to you". Again, when reciting the verse "and (those) who avenge themselves after being oppressed", he said, "That refers to you." [^2]
The People of Yemen Weep when they Hear the Qur'aan During the Khilaafah of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA)

Hadhrat Abu Saalih narrates that when some people from Yemen came to Madinah during the Khilaafah of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and heard the Qur'aan, they started weeping excessively. To this, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) remarked (in humility), "That is how we used to be, but then hearts started to harden." Hadhrat Abu Nu'aym explains that the phrase "hearts started to harden" means that their hearts strengthened and became content with the recognition of Allaah. [^3]
Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.1 Pg.224).
